title: How Condoms Work
summary: Josh and Chuck explain the history and mechanics of condoms, from ancient sheaths and linen wraps through animal-membrane and vulcanized rubber versions to modern latex condoms. They cover manufacturing steps and quality testing, proper use and disposal, effectiveness against pregnancy and STIs/HIV, social marketing and distribution in countries like Thailand, controversial anti-rape and spray-on condom ideas, and close with a listener mail about a listener's chronological music experiment.
topics: Measure B Los Angeles porn condom

segments.title: Opening banter and Measure B porn condom debate
segments.summary: The hosts open with off-topic banter about a speeding ticket, then discuss Measure B in Los Angeles County requiring condoms in porn filming, the industry's reaction, and a host's anecdote about scouting a porn stage.

segments.title: Early history of condoms
segments.summary: The hosts trace condom-like coverings back roughly fifteen thousand years to cave paintings, then to ancient Egypt, Greece, India, and Japan, the Roman era, Shakespeare's time, and syphilis prevention during the age of exploration.

segments.title: Animal membrane and vulcanized rubber condoms
segments.summary: Mid-1700s condoms made from animal intestine lining, their porosity and limited HIV protection, then Charles Goodyear's vulcanization of rubber and the fitted reusable rubber condoms of the later nineteenth century.

segments.title: Latex condom invention
segments.summary: Julius Fromm's process of dipping glass formers into liquid latex from the rubber tree and vulcanizing it, producing thinner, stronger condoms with longer shelf life; the hosts note that today's condoms are almost all latex.

segments.title: Condom anatomy and standards
segments.summary: The hosts describe the basic condom design with a reservoir tip and rolled rim, the standard dimensions for length, width and thickness, and why latex is nonporous and effective as a barrier.

segments.title: Manufacturing and lubricants
segments.summary: Latex is harvested from rubber trees and mixed with additives, then formers are dipped, vulcanized in a tunnel oven, washed, and powdered; lubricants are discussed, including spermicidal lube (nonoxynol-9) and its irritation risk.

segments.title: Quality testing and disposal
segments.summary: Condoms are tested for breakage and leaks through inflation, water-filled tests and electrical current tests; slippage is user error. The hosts also cover proper disposal, warning against flushing condoms down toilets.

segments.title: Proper condom use and effectiveness
segments.summary: Steps for storage, checking the package, orientation, unrolling and water-based lubricant, withdrawal, and avoiding double condoms or reuse. Effectiveness data from serodiscordant couples and pregnancy-rate figures are cited, along with STIs not prevented by condoms.

segments.title: Condom distribution, social marketing and Thailand
segments.summary: Government social marketing of condoms, the Thailand sex worker campaign that reduced STI cases, global condom production and shortfalls, and religious and cultural opposition.

segments.title: Female condoms, spray-on condoms, sizes and anti-rape condom
segments.summary: Polyurethane female condoms, a German sex educator's spray-on condom and small-size condom work, the South African anti-rape Rape-X device, and the goat oral-barrier population control aside.

segments.title: Listener mail: music experiment
segments.summary: A listener describes listening to his music chronologically by year of release over several months and the connection to past eras it created.

segments.title: Outro and contact info
segments.summary: The hosts ask for listener condom stories and give social media and email contact information.
